label: Diagram 2.2
caption: Diagram 2.2 Alternative arrangements for final exits | a. | b. | house with a storey more than 4.5m above ground level
description:
Two floor plans, a. and b., showing alternative arrangements for final exits from a protected stairway (see para 2.5). In the key, green lines are 'Fire resisting construction minimum REI 30' and 'Fd' is a 'Fire doorset minimum E 20'.

In a., the 'Protected stairway' is in the lower middle of the plan, enclosed by green lines. Three rooms open onto it through Fd doors: two side by side at the top and one on the left. A green arrow leads out through an opening in the right-hand wall to the 'Final exit'.

In b., the 'Protected stairway' runs across the middle of the plan, enclosed by green lines. At its right-hand end two Fd doors, one above the other, each lead to a 'Final exit', both shown by green arrows pointing right. A third Fd door is on the left of the plan.
model_description:
This diagram, titled "Diagram 2.2 Alternative arrangements for final exits," contains two separate parts, labelled 'a.' and 'b.', showing floor plans for a house with a storey more than 4.5m above ground level.

Part 'a.' shows a rectangular floor plan containing a 'Protected stairway'. A single green line, labelled 'Fire resisting construction minimum REI 30', forms a continuous enclosure around the stairway, except for one opening. This opening is marked 'Fd' and leads to a 'Final exit', which is indicated by a green arrow pointing out of the building. Another 'Fd' label, referring to 'Fire doorset minimum E 20', is placed on the door leading from the stairway into the main area of the floor plan.

Part 'b.' shows a rectangular floor plan with a 'Protected stairway' located towards the top centre. This stairway is enclosed by a green line representing 'Fire resisting construction minimum REI 30'. There are two 'Fd' labels on doors within this enclosure, both referring to 'Fire doorset minimum E 20'. These doors lead to two separate green arrows, both labelled 'Final exit', pointing outwards from the building in opposite directions. A note at the top left states 'See para 2.5'.
